operational_stresses: Each episode carries dense health and clinical nuance, so show notes, citations, clips, and follow-up content need review before they can be reused confidently.
A 50-minute expert conversation can become many smaller assets, but cutting, labeling, and writing them manually slows distribution.
Listeners may ask practical health questions after an episode, and the response needs to stay educational without drifting into medical advice.
Giveaways, product interest, app support, and podcast engagement can land in different systems unless intake and routing are cleaned up.
The first Frequency episode establishes a format that can scale, but only if every episode gets a repeatable post-production and compliance workflow.
hero_sub: A practical AI roadmap for Phi Health and the Frequency Podcast: turn expert conversations into researched episode prep, citation-aware show notes, compliant listener education, clips, giveaway follow-up, and app/shop support without slowing Scott down.
profile_note: You already have a strong content premise: learn from world-class voices about body, mind, recovery, and more healthy years. The opportunity is to turn every long-form conversation into a structured content, compliance, and listener-response system.

results.title: Health media brands are using AI to make expert content more useful without making unsupported claims.
results.sub: The best use case is not replacing your voice. It is giving your production workflow a research layer, a repurposing layer, and a claims-review layer so expert episodes travel farther with less manual drag.

cards.title: They prep better guest interviews
cards.desc: What they are doing: a research agent reads prior episodes, guest bios, and published claims before the interview. How it helps you: each Frequency conversation can start with sharper questions and cleaner context. How I would deliver it for you: the agent produces a guest dossier, topic map, careful claim notes, and listener-first questions before recording.

cards.title: They turn transcripts into trust-building assets
cards.desc: What they are doing: long transcripts become show notes, chapter summaries, clip captions, newsletters, and app content. How it helps you: a 50-minute expert episode becomes a week of useful education. How I would deliver it for you: a transcript agent pulls the key takeaways, chapter hooks, and careful disclaimers from every Frequency episode.

cards.title: They review claims before distribution
cards.desc: What they are doing: AI flags medical, supplement, and treatment claims that need softer language or a human review. How it helps you: your content stays educational instead of sounding like personal medical advice. How I would deliver it for you: a claims and citation review agent marks risky sentences before clips, emails, and shop copy go live.

cards.title: They route listeners while interest is fresh
cards.desc: What they are doing: listener questions, giveaway interest, app issues, and product questions get classified and answered quickly. How it helps you: engagement from the episode does not disappear into a general inbox. How I would deliver it for you: an intake agent sorts each message into podcast, product, app, guest, or support paths.

results.close: The win is a repeatable system around your existing voice: better prep before recording, cleaner production after recording, and faster listener follow-up once the episode is out.

agents.name: Guest Research and Interview Prep Agent
agents.desc: Before each Frequency recording, this agent prepares a guest dossier, topic map, interview angles, careful claim notes, and listener-first questions. It helps you ask sharper questions without turning the conversation into a generic wellness interview.
agents.outcome: Each episode starts with a stronger research base and a cleaner arc.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Guest Research and Interview Prep Agent for Scott Paul and Phi Health / Frequency Podcast. Build a guest dossier from approved public sources and internal notes. Output: guest background, strongest topics, five listener-first questions, three contrarian follow-ups, claim-risk notes, and a plain-language episode thesis. Keep the tone curious and rigorous. Do not invent credentials, studies, quotes, or medical facts. Flag any claim that needs human review.

agents.name: Transcript-to-Education Agent
agents.desc: After each episode, this agent turns the transcript into show notes, chapter summaries, listener takeaways, newsletter blocks, SEO summaries, app learning snippets, and a short disclaimer-safe recap.
agents.outcome: A 50-minute episode becomes a full education package instead of a single audio file.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Transcript-to-Education Agent for Phi Health / Frequency Podcast. Given an episode transcript, create chapter notes, a listener takeaway list, a newsletter section, SEO summary, short-form clip candidates, and app-friendly education snippets. Preserve the guest's meaning, avoid exaggeration, and use educational language. Never convert a general discussion into personal medical advice. Mark statements that need citations or clinician review.

agents.name: Claims and Citation Review Agent
agents.desc: This agent reviews episode notes, captions, emails, product education, and app content for health claims that need softer language, a citation, a disclaimer, or a human review before publishing.
agents.outcome: Your content keeps the trust of the listener while reducing avoidable claims risk.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Claims and Citation Review Agent for Phi Health. Review draft podcast notes, captions, emails, app copy, and product education for unsupported medical, supplement, treatment, cure, prevention, diagnosis, dosing, and outcome claims. Return a table with: original sentence, risk level, issue type, safer educational rewrite, citation needed yes/no, and human review needed yes/no. Do not approve claims you cannot support.

agents.name: Clip and Social Repurposing Agent
agents.desc: This agent finds high-value moments in every episode, writes hooks and captions, adapts the same idea for each channel, and keeps the language aligned with the claims review before posting.
agents.outcome: Frequency gets more reach from each recording without making Scott manually cut and rewrite every asset.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Clip and Social Repurposing Agent for Frequency Podcast. Given an episode transcript and timestamps, identify 12 short clip candidates with title, hook, caption, thumbnail phrase, audience, and claim-risk note. Keep each clip faithful to the source. Prefer curiosity and usefulness over sensational claims. Do not write disease-treatment promises, supplement promises, or clinician-like recommendations.

agents.name: Listener Intake and Giveaway Ops Agent
agents.desc: When someone comments, replies, enters a giveaway, asks about a guest, or needs the right Phi path, this agent classifies the message and drafts a safe response for review.
agents.outcome: Episode engagement gets routed while the listener still cares.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Listener Intake and Giveaway Ops Agent for Phi Health and Frequency Podcast. Classify incoming messages into podcast question, guest request, giveaway, Phi Stack/product education, app support, order/support, partnership, or medical advice request. Draft a short response for human approval. Use safe educational language, link to the right approved page when available, and route medical advice requests to a qualified professional instead of answering clinically.

agents.name: Product Education and Support Handoff Agent
agents.desc: This agent turns podcast interest into clear next steps: education, FAQ, shop/app support, or human escalation. It answers common questions carefully and never pretends to be a clinician.
agents.outcome: Listeners get help quickly without pushing AI into clinical advice.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Product Education and Support Handoff Agent for Phi Health. Answer common non-clinical questions using approved FAQ, shop, podcast, and app materials. Keep responses educational and concise. Never diagnose, prescribe, recommend dosing, or claim a product treats or prevents disease. If the user asks for personal medical guidance, advise them to consult a qualified clinician and route to human support if appropriate.
